title: Lesson 24. Algorithms without a computer
description: The Robot game: a computer follows commands exactly and in order

questions.explain: Commands in order for a computer.

questions.prompt: The robot does exactly what it is told, in order.
questions.explain: So it's important not to make mistakes.

questions.prompt: Match the mistake with what the robot did
questions.explain: A wrong command — a wrong move.
Steps in order make an algorithm.

questions.prompt: Which commands does the game robot know?

questions.text: A list of commands in order is called an ___.

questions.prompt: If a step is missing, the robot fills it in itself.
What do we do when the robot errs because of our algorithm?

learn.intro: Today you become a programmer, and your teacher becomes your robot!

slides.text: The robot knows only 3 commands: **"step forward"**, **"turn right"**, **"turn left"**. It does exactly what it is told and invents nothing.
Say "go there" — the robot stands still: no such command. Say "step forward" facing a wall — it bumps into it. A bug in the program!
A list of commands in order is called an **algorithm**. A **program** is an algorithm for a computer.

check.explain: An algorithm is a list of steps in order.

slides.text: Write the algorithm "How to make a sandwich". The robot follows it literally: "Spread the butter". With what? You never said take a knife!
Fix the algorithm — add the missing steps. Then swap roles.

check.prompt: Why did the robot "spread butter with its hands"?
options: The step "take a knife" was missing
check.explain: The robot only does what is written.
